chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from al-ʿAbbas, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbbad, from Khirash, from some of our companions, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, “May I be made your ransom, these opponents against us say: when the sky is overcast upon us or it becomes dark over us, and we cannot recognize the sky, then we and you are equal in ijtihad.” So he said, “It is not as they say. When that happens, then let him perform salat toward four directions.”

key_terms.أَطْبَقَتْ: became fully covered over, referring to the sky being obscured
key_terms.الِاجْتِهَادِ: independent judgment used here in the sense of trying to determine direction
key_terms.الْمُخَالِفِينَ: the opponents or dissenters referred to in the discussion

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if the qiblah is unclear on a cloudy or dark day?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who is uncertain about the qiblah on a cloudy or dark day. Imam Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام rejects the claim that such a case reduces everyone to the same conjecture, and instructs that salat be performed toward four directions to ensure fulfillment of the obligation.
